@graph.name: TvL with HBT does not remove PFOA over two weeks; the 64 to 67 % concentration fall at 0.1 uM is recovered in full on extraction
@graph.description: Does Trametes versicolor laccase with HBT degrade PFOA or PFOS under conditions where it transforms carbamazepine?
@graph.nrr:successCriteria: A significant loss of PFAA mass relative to untreated control, confirmed by extraction of the whole reactor.

nrr:applicabilityConditions.system: laccase mediator systems with nitroxyl (N-OH or N-oxyl) mediators in aerated batch reactors at 30 °C
nrr:applicabilityConditions.enzymes: Trametes versicolor laccase (MilliporeSigma) for the TvL experiments; Agaricus bisporus and a native white-rot laccase in the screen; the Pleurotus ostreatus laccase of the prior reports was not available
nrr:applicabilityConditions.substrateConcentrations: 1 uM (screen and two-week experiment) and 0.1 uM (96 h and 24 h experiments)
nrr:applicabilityConditions.matrices: 10 mM CuSO4 pH 5 or 50 mM sodium malonate pH 4.5
nrr:applicabilityConditions.duration: 24 h to 28 days with repeated enzyme and mediator dosing
nrr:applicabilityConditions.analysis: LC-MS/MS, Agilent Triple Quad 6460A, negative electrospray, multiple reaction monitoring; isotope dilution with mass-labelled 13C PFAAs at 2 to 5 ug/L; calibration range 0.2 to 10 ug/L; samples diluted to a target of 10 ug/L; delay column after the purge valve; mobile-phase blanks every 10 samples (Text S2)
nrr:applicabilityConditions.note: the negative is about detectable degradation under these conditions; sorption to the enzyme is shown to mimic up to about 60 % apparent removal when only the aqueous phase is sampled

nrr:cost.note: batch reactors in triplicate; the longest experiment 28 days; no monetary cost reported

nrr:provenanceNotes: The two refuted findings and the informative negative sit in one attempt because they are the same question asked at two concentrations; the apparent loss at 0.1 uM is what a less careful study would have published.

nrr:aiUseDeclaration.statement: The article makes no statement about the use of AI tools.

nrr:confidence.basis: surrogate positive control passed; untreated controls; triplicates; full mass recovery

@graph.nrr:outcomeSummary: monitoring PFOA treatment with six doses of 1 unit/mL TvL and 1 mM HBT over the course of 2 weeks did not indicate significant removal compared to an untreated control (p = 0.29; two-tailed t test) At 0.1 uM, a 64 % decrease in PFOA concentration and a 67 % decrease in PFOS concentration at the 24 hour time point after two doses, but 99 +/- 14 % of the PFOA mass and 111 +/- 11 % of the PFOS mass were recovered in the extracted solutions, suggesting that the decrease in concentration was likely due to physical phenomena (e.g., sorption)

nrr:effect.metric: PFOA concentration relative to untreated control after two weeks
nrr:effect.comparedTo: untreated control; the prior report claimed >20 % removal after 10 days

positive.label: carbamazepine (CBZ) as surrogate substrate with TvL and HBT
positive.note: a different substrate run in a separate reactor set with the same enzyme, mediator and buffer, not an arm of the same experiment; it shows the enzyme-mediator system was oxidatively active

@graph.nrr:sensitivity: LC-MS/MS isotope-dilution quantification with a 0.2 to 10 ug/L calibration range (Text S2) in triplicate reactors with standard deviations reported; the effect sought was the previously reported >20 % removal at 10 days (PFOA) and >20 % at 20 days, >30 % at 30 days (PFOS). The ingest treats the stated quantification range and the stated expected effect size as the sensitivity statement; the article reports no formal power analysis.

nrr:evidence.label: Results paragraph 2; SI Figure S4
nrr:evidence.quote: monitoring PFOA treatment with six doses of 1 unit/mL TvL and 1 mM HBT over the course of 2 weeks did not indicate significant removal compared to an untreated control (p = 0.29; two-tailed t test)

@graph.nrr:nearestPriorResult: Luo et al. 2015, laccase-catalyzed degradation of perfluorooctanoic acid (ES&T Lett. 2, 198-203): >20 % PFOA removal after 10 days
